name: Tree
description: A hierarchical list of folders, files or records: groups that open and close with a chevron, one selected row and arrow-key navigation. Use it to browse a folder or file structure, or as a picker inside a card.

classes.ayy-tree: Root <ul role="tree">. Its aria-label names it ("Folders"). <ayy-tree> wraps it with display: contents.
classes.ayy-tree__item: One <li role="treeitem">. Carries aria-level, aria-selected on every node, aria-expanded only on parents, and a roving tabindex: exactly one visible item is 0, the rest -1. aria-disabled="true" makes it unselectable.
classes.ayy-tree__row: The clickable row inside the item: toggle, optional icon and label. Hover and selected washes sit here, and so does the focus ring.
classes.ayy-tree__toggle: The decorative <span aria-hidden="true"> holding the chevron. Clicking it opens or closes the group without selecting the row; the treeitem's aria-expanded carries the state.
classes.ayy-tree__icon: An optional decorative icon before the label (an <svg class="ayy-icon ayy-tree__icon"> drawn by Icon or iconSvg). Muted, and text colour on the selected row.
classes.ayy-tree__label: The node's label. It takes the leftover width, wraps anywhere so a long unbroken name never scrolls the tree sideways, and is not the accessible name: the item's aria-label is.
classes.ayy-tree__group: A nested <ul role="group"> of child items, indented by --ayy-space-5 (--ayy-space-4 with --compact). Put hidden on it while its parent is aria-expanded="false"; connectTree keeps the two in step.
classes.ayy-tree--compact: Tighter rows at the sm control height, small control text, a 16px indent and a 16px toggle.

default.looks: Rows at the md control height, with a muted chevron and icon, the label in the text colour, and --ayy-space-0-5 between rows.

hover.looks: A --ayy-color-wash behind the row and, over the chevron, a --ayy-color-wash-hover and the text colour. A selected row keeps its stronger wash.

pressed.none: No pressed look: the click selects the row at once.

focus.looks: A 2px --ayy-color-ring outline on the row, inset by 2px. Hidden after pointer use by trackInputModality()'s pointer mode.

disabled.looks: --ayy-opacity-disabled and a not-allowed cursor; clicking selects and activates nothing. Forced colours: GrayText.

selected.when: aria-selected="true" on the treeitem, set by a click, Space, or your selectedId
selected.looks: A --ayy-color-wash-hover behind the row, the text colour and a medium weight; its icon takes the text colour. Forced colours: a Highlight outline.

error.none: No error state; show problems beside the tree (Alert or FieldError).

loading.none: No loading state; put Skeleton rows in the tree's place while it loads.

expanded.looks: Its group is not hidden and the chevron turns down: rotate(90deg) in LTR, the mirror in RTL (--_ayy-dir). The treeitem's aria-expanded, not the decorative toggle, carries the state.

sizes.density: Rows are at least the md control height (32px compact, 40px comfortable, 44px touch) with --ayy-control-text-md; --compact uses the sm height (28, 32, 40) and --ayy-control-text-sm. The toggle is 20px (16px compact), so touch density keeps a comfortable target.
sizes.width: Fills its container. Child groups indent by --ayy-space-5 (--ayy-space-4 compact) using padding-inline-start, so they indent from the right in RTL. Labels take the leftover width and wrap anywhere.

js: treeClass({ compact?, className? }) → root classes; treeItemClass, treeRowClass, treeToggleClass, treeIconClass, treeLabelClass, treeGroupClass constants; treeChevronIcon (the ArrowRight01Icon SVG, directional); connectTree(root, { onSelect?, onActivate?, onToggle? }) → { focus(id?), destroy() } — expansion, single selection, roving tabindex and keyboard movement on plain markup.

element.children: Wraps the <ul role="tree"> and makes it work: the toggle opens and closes a group, a row selects, double-click or Enter activates, and the arrow keys, Home and End move the roving tab stop. focus(id) moves to a node from code.

events.ayy-select: { id } — a row was clicked or Space was pressed on it.
events.ayy-activate: { id } — a row was double-clicked or Enter was pressed on it (open the file or folder).
events.ayy-toggle: { id, expanded } — a group was opened (true) or closed (false).

Tree.renders: <ul class="ayy-tree" role="tree" aria-label> with a <li class="ayy-tree__item" role="treeitem"> per node, a __row inside it, and a nested <ul class="ayy-tree__group" role="group" hidden> for children

props.label: string — accessible name of the tree ("Folders")
props.nodes: TreeNode[] — { id: string; label: string; icon?: ReactNode; children?: TreeNode[]; disabled?: boolean }, nested in display order
props.expandedIds / defaultExpandedIds: string[] — open group ids; expandedIds makes it controlled, defaultExpandedIds sets the starting ones
props.onExpandedChange: (ids: string[]) => void — a group opened or closed
props.selectedId / defaultSelectedId: string — the selected node; selectedId makes it controlled, defaultSelectedId sets the starting one
props.onSelectedChange: (id: string | null) => void — a row was selected
props.onActivate: (id: string) => void — a row was double-clicked or Enter was pressed
props.compact: boolean — tighter rows, a smaller indent and the small control text

a11y: The tree is a <ul role="tree"> with a name (label in React, aria-label in HTML); each node is a <li role="treeitem"> with aria-level, and children sit in a <ul role="group">.

aria-expanded is only on parents and aria-selected is on every node, so the state is announced rather than drawn only as a wash. The toggle is decorative (aria-hidden) and the item's aria-label is the node label, never the toggle.

One visible item has tabindex="0" and the rest -1 (a roving tab stop). Tab enters the tree on the selected node, then the arrow keys, Home and End move through the visible nodes: Right closes an open group or opens a closed one and steps into its first child, Left closes an open group or moves to the parent.
Enter activates a node and Space selects it. Double-click activates too. A composing IME and fields inside a row (a rename input) keep their keys.
aria-disabled="true" keeps a node readable and reachable by the keyboard while it refuses selection and activation; colour is backed by opacity and, in High Contrast, GrayText.
Long labels wrap inside the row instead of scrolling the tree sideways, and touch density raises the rows to the 44px target.
do: Use a tree to browse a nested structure: folders and files, a page hierarchy, categories or a project's contents.
Keep ids stable and pass them as expandedIds/selectedId when the rest of the screen shows the same folder (a picker in a card, a split view).
Pair the chevron with the label on the same row and let the label wrap; never truncate a folder name to make a narrow tree fit.
dont: Don't use a tree for a flat list — use List; for sections that collapse in place use Accordion.
Don't use it as the app's main navigation — use App shell or Navbar.

Don't pack several controls into a row: the tree ignores clicks inside a button, link or field, but the row's job is selection. Put a bigger set of actions in a detail pane or a menu outside the tree.
Don't nest more than four or five levels; show a breadcrumb or a detail pane instead.
